subject: Urgent: LedgerBridge reserved throughput shortfall — immediate remediation & exec ask
messages:
From: Ravi Shah <ravi@ledgerbridge.com>
To: support@redwood.com
Cc: Clara Nguyen <clara@ledgerbridge.com>
Date: 2028-03-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: Production: sudden latency and 5xx spike on reserved pool (urgent)

Team,

We started seeing a sustained latency spike and ~8% 5xx errors on our /v1/generate path since 08:45 PST. This is hitting our critical payment flows — we have a queued backlog and customers are timing out. Per our reserved capacity in the contract (LB-2027-78) we should have stable throughput; this looks like the dedicated GPU pool is saturated.

Can you confirm whether this is a capacity saturation, noisy neighbor, or a routing issue? We need an ETA on mitigation and whether you can authorize emergency burst capacity today.

Ravi
Head of Platform, LedgerBridge

--
attachments: none
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>

Cc: support@redwood.com, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-01T09:25:00Z
Subject: Re: Production: sudden latency and 5xx spike on reserved pool (urgent)

Ravi — thanks for flagging and I’m sorry for the disruption. We’ve elevated to SEV-2 and stood up an incident bridge. Short update:

- Initial telemetry shows sustained token-queue depth increase and elevated tail latency on the dedicated pool backing LedgerBridge’s reservation.
- Engineering is running a hotpath inspection now (Jonas + infra on the bridge).
- I’ve requested emergency burst capacity authorization from the capacity ops team; I’ll update in the next 15–30 minutes.

Immediate ask from you: if you can share a short list of recent critical wallet/payment endpoints and any traffic shaping windows, we’ll prioritize routing and KV-cache priming for those prefixes.

We will not make config changes to your pinned reservation without your sign-off — will propose fallbacks first.

Olga
Senior Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference

Date: 2028-03-01T09:40:00Z
Subject: INTERNAL: LedgerBridge reserved pool saturation — immediate triage steps

Team — bridge recap and required actions (timeline in parentheses):

1) Hotpath triage (Jonas, now): root-cause snapshot attached (capacity-snapshot-20280301.csv). Initial signal: sustained KV-cache miss rate uptick + increased long-running attention kernels on p4d-plat-3.
2) Short-term mitigation (David, next 10–20m): enable token-level prefilling and apply route to fallback variant (gpt-redwood-64q-compat) for non-critical prefixes to free headroom for payment endpoints. Need engineering sign-off to route 20% of traffic.
3) Burst authorization (Marissa, next 30m): request emergency burst of +2 reserved GPUs to the cluster for 2 hours. If approved we can target steady state within ~12 minutes after allocation.
4) Customer comms (Naomi, draft within 15m): short note with ETA and temporary mitigations. Ravi is on the bridge.
5) Longer-term follow-ups: add a tuned autoscale policy to this reservation and run a workload quantization analysis.

Decision needed: Marissa, please confirm ability to authorize +2 GPUs and whether we need a credit approval from Finance (expected cost $X for 2 hours). We should also confirm whether legal needs to sign an SLA exception for burst usage.

I’ll keep Ravi updated on the bridge.

Olga

--

Olga — I’m authorizing the +2 GPU emergency burst for LedgerBridge for 2 hours. Finance: please treat as operational credit (Marissa approves provisional credit up to $6,000 for this window).

David/Jonas — proceed with the routing change: route non-critical sampling to the fallback variant, prioritize prefixes Ravi will send. Confirm when route is live.

Naomi — draft to send to Ravi and Clara: include ETA on remediation (target 12 minutes after allocation + ongoing monitoring). Suggest offering a one-week service credit if we miss SLA for the week.

Marissa
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference

Brief update from our side: after you routed critical prefixes and brought the emergency burst up, tail latency dropped back within acceptable bounds and 5xx fell to <0.5%. We appreciate the temporary credit offer; Clara will coordinate a short post-incident review next week and we’ll expect the MAP and a follow-up plan for autoscale + quantization adjustments. Please include the capacity snapshot and the proposed SLA exception in the packet.

Date: 2028-03-02T15:40:00Z
Subject: INTERNAL: Exec summary and next steps for LedgerBridge incident

Executive note for the record:

- Incident summary: Dedicated GPU pool supporting LedgerBridge hit sustained saturation during morning peak traffic (KV-cache miss storm + heavy attention kernel tails). Result: elevated latency and transient 5xxs; customer experienced ~9m payment degradation window.
- Immediate remediation: emergency +2 GPU burst (Marissa approved) + routing to fallback variant for non-critical prefixes. Impact: service restored to SLA bounds; ongoing monitoring in place.
- Customer ask: MAP and concrete timeline for autoscale/quantization changes. They requested a post-incident review next week.
- Proposed exec asks: 1) approve a formal one-week service credit capped at $6,000 (pre-approved by Marissa), 2) prioritize a targeted autoscale policy for this reservation in the next sprint, 3) allocate an applied-research slot for workload quantization and kernel selection.

Next steps: Naomi will send public-facing comms and the MAP doc (attached). David and Jonas — file a root-cause writeup and remediation runbook by EOD tomorrow. I’ll sync with Legal about the SLA exception language.

Olga
Senior Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
